Afni's chief information security officer is quoted. Yubico (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-22, opens in new tab)
How confidence is setIt follows the kind of evidence, not judgement.
  • The customer's own statement (high confidence at most): The organisation says so itself: its press release, website, annual report or a named executive on the record.
  • Regulatory or securities filing (high confidence at most): A filing by the customer or the vendor names the relationship.
  • Independent press (high confidence at most): Editorially independent reporting describes the deployment.
  • Joint announcement (medium confidence at most): A press release issued with the vendor, usually with a quote from the customer.
  • Vendor case study (medium confidence at most): The vendor's published customer story naming the organisation.
  • Vendor mention only (low confidence at most): A logo, a customer list or a passing mention by the vendor, with nothing from the customer.
  • An organisation that also holds a stake in the vendor is labelled “Investor and customer” and is never rated above medium.
  • A partnership is listed as a partner, not a customer.

Reputation

Adverse items are attributed to their sources and need one primary source or two independent ones before they are published.

Reputation
Regulatory actionsNo public evidence Ask the vendor: Has Yubico been subject to any regulatory investigation, order or penalty in the last five years, and what was the outcome?
LitigationNo public evidence Ask the vendor: Is Yubico party to any material litigation or dispute, and what is its status?
Security incidentsYubico published advisory YSA-2024-03 on 2024-09-03: a side-channel flaw in a chip supplier's cryptographic library allows recovery of ECDSA private keys from YubiKey 5 Series and related devices with firmware before 5.7 by an attacker with physical possession and specialised equipment; Yubico rated it Moderate (CVSS 4.9) and said firmware cannot be upgraded, so older keys remain affected. Advisory YSA-2025-02 of 2025-04-02 reported a Low-rated protocol conformance flaw fixed in firmware 5.7.4. Two advisories in 2026 concern software libraries. No intrusion into Yubico's own systems was found in the pages read. Questions to ask the vendor (5)

  1. How many organisations buy YubiKeys directly or by subscription today, and how many are banks?
    A customer count indicates how widely the product is deployed.
  2. Which analyst evaluations of authentication products has Yubico been placed in over the last two years, and where?
    Analyst placements are one input to market presence.
  3. Has Yubico been subject to any regulatory investigation, order or penalty in the last five years, and what was the outcome?
    Regulatory action against an authentication vendor bears on a bank's own supervisory standing.
  4. Is Yubico party to any material litigation or dispute, and what is its status?
    Material litigation can divert resources or signal product or conduct problems.
  5. Has Yubico lost any large financial-services customer in the last three years, and why?
    Loss of large customers can signal product or service problems.

  4. 2025-12-17 · leadership change Yubico
    Yubico chief executive steps down; chief operating officer becomes acting CEO

    Yubico announced on 2025-12-17 that chief executive Mattias Danielsson was stepping down after about sixteen years with the company and that chief operating officer Jerrod Chong had been appointed acting CEO. Yubico (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-21, opens in new tab)

  5. 2025-04-02 · vulnerability disclosure Yubico
    Yubico discloses a low-severity FIDO protocol conformance flaw in YubiKey firmware

    Yubico published advisory YSA-2025-02 (CVE-2025-29991) on 2025-04-02: YubiKey 5 Series, 5 FIPS Series, Bio Series and Security Key Series firmware 5.4.1 to 5.7.3 checked only a 16-byte signature where FIDO PIN/UV Auth Protocol Two requires 32 bytes. Yubico rated it Low (CVSS 2.2), reported no known exploitation and said firmware 5.7.4, released 2025-04-01, addresses it. Yubico (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-21, opens in new tab)

  6. 2024-12-05 · corporate restructuring Yubico
    Yubico shares begin trading on Nasdaq Stockholm's main market

    Yubico's investor pages state that its share has been listed on Nasdaq Stockholm since 2024-12-05, following approval announced on 2024-11-28. The investor site also carries a section on an earlier listing on Nasdaq First North Growth Market. A change of listing venue, not of control.
